content.value_statement: Project teams lose clarity when key domain terms drift across code and conversations. This skill helps define vocabulary, context maps, and ADRs as decisions emerge.
actual_capabilities: Creates or updates CONTEXT.md when domain terms are resolved.
Uses CONTEXT-MAP.md to handle repositories with multiple contexts.
Challenges vague or conflicting domain terms against the glossary.
Suggests ADRs only for hard-to-reverse trade-off decisions.
Applies supplied formats for context files and lightweight ADRs.
limitations: It depends on user confirmation for unclear domain boundaries.
It does not replace formal architecture review or stakeholder validation.
It records glossary and ADR documentation, not implementation specifications.
It may need repository access to compare stated behavior with code.

use_cases.title: Align Product Language
use_cases.description: Define clear names for business concepts before product requirements become inconsistent.

use_cases.title: Maintain Context Boundaries
use_cases.description: Separate terms, ownership, and relationships across multiple bounded contexts in a repository.

use_cases.title: Record Architecture Decisions
use_cases.description: Capture important trade-off decisions in short ADRs when the rationale should remain visible.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Glossary
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project or feature area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a CONTEXT.md glossary for this project. Ask clarifying questions before adding any domain terms.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Term Conflict
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate cleanup when teams use different words for the same concept.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our current domain terms and identify conflicts. Recommend one canonical term and list terms we should avoid.

prompt_templates.title: Map Contexts
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced modeling for repositories with multiple business areas.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me decide whether this repository needs a CONTEXT-MAP.md. Identify contexts, ownership, and relationships between them.

prompt_templates.title: Decide on an ADR
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced decision capture for architecture trade-offs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this architecture decision against the ADR criteria. If it qualifies, draft a short ADR with context, decision, and rationale.

output: Question to resolve: Does every user represent a customer?

output_examples.input: Ordering and Billing now communicate through domain events.
output_examples.output: ADR suggested. The decision changes integration coupling and future readers may need the trade-off rationale.

output_examples.input: Our repository contains Ordering, Billing, and Fulfillment areas.
output: Create a context map because multiple contexts exist.
Record each context path and summarize how they relate.
Ask which context owns shared customer terminology.

best_practices: Confirm ambiguous terms with domain experts before recording them.
Keep glossary definitions short and focused on business meaning.
Create ADRs only when the decision is hard to reverse and surprising.
anti_patterns: Do not turn CONTEXT.md into a technical specification.
Do not record general programming concepts as domain language.
Do not create ADRs for obvious or easily reversible choices.

faq.question: Does this skill write production code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on domain language, context maps, and architecture decision records.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when terms are unclear, contexts overlap, or an important architecture decision needs a written record.

faq.question: Can it support multiple bounded contexts?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses CONTEXT-MAP.md to identify contexts, locations, and relationships when a repository has several domains.

faq.question: Will it challenge my terminology?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to call out vague, overloaded, or conflicting terms before they become shared language.

faq.question: What is stored in CONTEXT.md?
faq.answer: CONTEXT.md stores glossary terms and avoided alternatives. It should not contain implementation details.

faq.question: When does it suggest an ADR?
faq.answer: It suggests an ADR when a decision is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and based on real trade-offs.
